sections.title: The measure, grain and drawn threshold
sections.text: The Odia transcription describes the first Margasira Thursday through a prepared grain measure, new paddy and rice-paste designs. Areca nuts, sugarcane, radish and banana belong to its ritual arrangement. This passage records objects and preparation, not a verified household menu.

sections.title: A separate Sudasa passage
sections.text: The text then explicitly introduces Sudasa Brata: a Thursday coinciding with the bright tenth. Its ten-knotted thread and ten manda with banana, coconut and chhena follow that transition. They cannot automatically be assigned to every Manabasa Thursday; quantities and practice need edition and household checks.

sections.title: Return on the condition of shared food
sections.text: At the close, Lakshmi confronts the brothers for accepting food after condemning her as Chandala. Before returning, she demands mutual feeding across the caste hierarchy; Jagannath agrees. The passage makes shared food a condition of reconciliation within the story. It does not prove that historical discrimination ended.
